# Command reference

Every command, subcommand and flag the `texec` binary accepts, in the order
`texec help` walks the tree. Use it to confirm a flag name or a default; the
pages next to it explain what the commands are for.

Every command reads the same configuration as the server, so point it at the right
configuration file with `--config` when you run more than one instance on a host.
See [Configuration](../configuration.md) for the lookup order.

<a id="global-flags"></a>

## Global flags

These are accepted by every command.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--config` | string | — | Configuration file path |
| `--debug-filter` | string | — | Debug namespace filter (only with DEBUG level), e.g. 'runner,task_*' or '*,-db' |
| `--log-level` | string | — | Log level: DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, FATAL, PANIC |
| `--no-config` | bool | — | Don't use configuration file |

<a id="texec-migrate"></a>

## `texec migrate`

Execute migrations

```
texec migrate
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--apply-to` | string | — | Apply to specific version |
| `--err-log-size` | int | `0` | Error log size |
| `--merge-existing-users` | bool | — | Reuse existing users matched by username instead of failing on conflict |
| `--skip-task-output` | bool | — | Skip task output importing during migration |
| `--undo-to` | string | — | Undo to specific version |

<a id="texec-vaults"></a>

## `texec vaults`

Manage access keys and other secrets

```
texec vaults
```

Aliases: `vault`.

| Subcommand | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`texec vaults check`](#texec-vaults-check) | Report which key id encrypts each stored secret |
| [`texec vaults rekey`](#texec-vaults-rekey) | Re-encrypt all stored secrets under the active encryption key |

<a id="texec-vaults-check"></a>

## `texec vaults check`

Read-only. Reports, per key id, how many locally stored Access Key secrets, alert credentials and the JWT signing key it encrypts, plus the JWT option's status. Use it after `vault rekey` to confirm a retired key is safe to remove: a key with zero references can be deleted from the keyset. Rows whose key id is missing from the keyset are flagged and cause a non-zero exit.

```
texec vaults check
```

<a id="texec-vaults-rekey"></a>

## `texec vaults rekey`

Re-encrypt all locally stored secrets (access keys, alert credentials and the JWT signing key) under the active key, stamping its key id into each value.  Zero-downtime rotation:   1. Add a new key to the keyset (a file in keys_folder, or a keys: entry) and      point active.access_key (or access_key_file) at it; reload applies it      within keys_poll_interval, or send `kill -HUP <pid>`.   2. Run `vault rekey` to re-encrypt existing data to the new key.   3. Run `vault check`; once the old key shows 0 rows it is safe to remove.  Legacy: `vault rekey --old-key <old-key>` decrypts un-prefixed data with an explicit old key.

```
texec vaults rekey
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--backup` | string | — | Write a backup of current access key ciphertexts to this file before re-encrypting |
| `--old-key` | string | — | Explicit old encryption key (legacy single-key migration; not needed when the old key is configured as a secondary) |
| `--rollback` | string | — | Restore access key ciphertexts from a backup file instead of re-encrypting |
